domain_label: Yarn Quality Spec & Acceptance — The Cost-of-Quality Economics
purpose: A method for specifying and accepting sweater yarn as a contract, not a lab: defining the spinning-stage quality determinants (staple length, twist/TPI, ply, micron/dpf, blend ratio) and tracing how each surfaces in the finished sweater; treating pilling as the #1 post-purchase failure and return driver and showing how fibre + twist + gauge + anti-pill finish jointly control it; pinning evenness/defect metrics (CV%, IPI, neps, thin/thick) to USTER percentiles; and expressing the whole as an enforceable purchase order — count-anchored, 25%-USTER-claused (never 5% on mainstream acrylic), ICI-Pilling-Box >=3-4-after-home-wash-gated, fibre-composition-verified, AQL-sampled — with a formula node that recomputes expected pilling/return risk against the spec dials. The micro-brand posture is contractual QC, never in-house metrology; every price/MOQ/throughput/lead-time band is a labeled estimate, never a fake-precise fact.
assumptions: no in-house USTER tester or pilling box is owned; a USTER-class evenness tester is six-figure-USD class (exact list price UNKNOWN), so quality is enforced contractually via the spinner's lab or a third-party spot-check, not by metrology we own

the three-article line is fixed (A1 cotton-blend 12GG 12-month core; A2 fine-acrylic 7-12GG value driver; A3 merino/lambswool 7-12GG seasonal premium capsule), and acrylic (A2) is the worst pilling offender the spec must defend hardest
every quality determinant is set per article tier, not globally; the same PO clause means a different number on A2 acrylic than on A3 merino

USTER STATISTICS percentile language is the common PO grading vocabulary; 25% USTER is the achievable mainstream-acrylic/cotton bar, while 5% USTER on a mass acrylic lot is unquotable or luxury-priced
pilling is the single highest-leverage failure to design out, and the post-home-wash ICI Pilling Box grade (not the dry off-loom grade) is what predicts returns

the single highest-leverage confirmation for the uncertain quality numbers is a PPS swatch tested at a third-party lab against the exact construction (fibre x twist x gauge), plus a per-lot USTER report from the spinner
every price/MOQ/throughput/lead-time figure is a labeled estimate with confidence, never a stated fact; no named-firm figure is asserted as fact
exclusions: fibre selection and count-to-gauge design choices for the three articles — covered by the fibre-line KB (kb1)
where to buy, MOQ negotiation, dyed-vs-greige and importer logistics — covered by the sourcing/supply KB (kb2)
finishing-process chemistry (cellulase bio-polish, singeing, heat-set, mercerising) execution detail — covered by the finishing KB (T6)
the cheaper-than-USTER thread-checker device design — defined as parameters here but built in the inspection KB (T5)
knit-stage construction levers (stitch density, loop length, gauge tightness) as machine settings — referenced here as quality inputs but owned by the machines/construction KB (T3/T8)
any fabricated actual lab result, tester price, or named-spinner quality figure stated as audited fact
source_description: labeled estimates, cited standards, and dimensional identities for specifying and accepting sweater yarn, grounded in the yarn deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), the shared scope glossary (SCOPE_GLOSSARY.md), and the reconciled yarn brief; quality determinants and pilling defence draw on textile-metrology standards (USTER STATISTICS percentiles, ISO 12945-1 ICI Pilling Box, ISO 2062 tenacity, AQL sampling) plus tagged industry-lore on anti-pill/compact-spinning levers, while every price/MOQ/throughput band is a triangulated estimate refused as a current point-anchor
source_citation: USTER Technologies USTER STATISTICS percentile methodology (5%/25%/50% USTER on CVm%, IPI); ISO 12945-1 (ICI Pilling Box) and ISO 12945-2 (Martindale) pilling grade 1-5; standard textile metrology for CV% (CVm), U% (CV% ~= 1.25 x U%), IPI (thin -50% / thick +50% / nep +200% per 1000 m), hairiness H/S3, tenacity cN/tex (ISO 2062), count-CV; AQL acceptable-quality-limit sampling (standard apparel QC, T5); USITC duty lines (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32%) for the blend-ratio/duty exposure; dimensional count identities (Tex = 1000/Nm = 590.5/Ne; Nm = 1.693 x Ne); SCOPE_GLOSSARY.md Sections 1/2/5; yarn DEEPDIVE.md sections 1d, 4a-4d; reconciled.md

glossary.definition: One of the five mostly-independent quality determinants set at the spinning stage — staple length, twist (TPM/TPI + S/Z or twist-multiplier K), ply, fibre fineness (micron for animal, denier-per-filament for synthetic), and blend ratio — each mapping to one thing the customer feels in the finished sweater.

The 1-5 lab rating (5 = no pill, 1 = severe) from the ICI Pilling Box wear test (ISO 12945-1); the objective gate behind any anti-pill claim, contractually required at >= 3-4 after >= 1 home-wash cycle because washing drops the grade and the post-wash grade predicts returns.

The rule that the pilling acceptance grade is read after at least one domestic wash cycle, not on the dry off-loom fabric, because washing lowers the grade and the post-wash value is what correlates with real-world returns.

Where a yarn sits versus global production per parameter on USTER STATISTICS; 25% USTER = better than 75% of world production. The common PO grading language; 25% USTER on CVm% + IPI is the achievable mainstream-acrylic/cotton bar and 5% USTER on a mass acrylic lot is unquotable or luxury-priced.

Thin places (-50%) + thick places (+50%) + neps (+200%) per 1000 m at standard sensitivities; the point-defect/cleanliness number read alongside CV%, where high IPI predicts visible faults and knitting stops.

glossary.term: CV% / CVm (coefficient of variation of mass)
glossary.definition: Std-dev / mean of yarn mass per unit length (%); the headline evenness number, lower = more even and cleaner-knitting, and the figure buyers anchor a lot grade on (legacy U% converts as CV% ~= 1.25 x U%).

A folded yarn whose opposing singles twists (S vs Z) cancel so a knit panel does not skew, torque or spiral; the PO must require it because under-twist pills and over-twist feels wiry and causes spirality (the twisted-side-seam defect).

A supplier quietly shifting the fibre ratio away from the specified blend (e.g. 70/30 toward more acrylic) — simultaneously a cost-down on the buyer and, as importer of record, a duty-misdeclaration exposure (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% vs wool 6110.11 ~16%, with acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% the outlier); controlled by a +/-% tolerance and fibre-composition test in the PO.

The micro-brand posture that quality is enforced through PO clauses, the spinner's lab, and third-party spot-checks rather than owned test equipment, because a USTER-class tester is six-figure-USD class (exact price UNKNOWN); the spec is a contract, not a lab we run.

A recomputable index that combines the spec dials (fibre, staple, twist, ply, dpf/micron, gauge, anti-pill finish) into an expected post-wash pilling grade and a relative return-risk estimate, recomputed whenever a dial moves; magnitude is a labeled estimate, never a promised customer number.

nodes.definition: Catalog the five mostly-independent spinning-stage quality determinants and trace each to the thing the customer feels: (1) staple length — longer fibre -> less pill, stronger, smoother, so name a minimum staple (mm) or fibre grade in the PO, not just the count; (2) twist (TPM/TPI + S/Z, or twist-multiplier K) — the strength-vs-softness optimum, with under-twist pilling and breaking and over-twist feeling wiry and causing spirality, knitwear-soft ~ K3, require balanced ply; (3) ply — 2-ply binds better than singles, which skew/torque a flat panel (a QC reject), so confirm singles count + ply + ends-fed (2/30 vs 1/30 is a doubling error); (4) fibre fineness (micron for animal, denier-per-filament for synthetic) — the counter-intuitive dial: finer = softer but pills MORE and is weaker, so spec a micron ceiling (e.g. <= 19.5 um) not the word merino, and an anti-pill/higher-dpf acrylic grade (~2.5 dpf) not the cheapest 1D; (5) blend ratio +/- tolerance — the margin/positioning/duty lever (its own node). These five dials are the vocabulary the whole spec is written in.

included: each dial's direction and customer-felt outcome
excluded: pilling mechanism in depth (its own node)
how each dial is written as a PO clause (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming five independent dials lets the spec set each to the article tier instead of a vague midweight adjective
pros.example: an acrylic value article gets higher-dpf + higher twist while a merino capsule gets a micron ceiling, from the same five-dial template

cons.claim: The dials are only mostly independent, so optimizing one can move another (twist up hardens hand)
cons.example: raising twist to cut pilling also makes the yarn feel wiry, trading the pilling dial against the hand the customer feels

failure_modes: specifying count alone and leaving staple, twist and dpf blank in a naive PO
treating finer fibre as unambiguously better and ignoring that it pills more and is weaker
acceptance_tests: all five determinants are named, each tied to a customer-felt outcome with its direction, and the finer=softer-but-pills-more caveat is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: a PPS swatch reveals a dial drives a defect more than assumed
a fibre grade or anti-pill acrylic dpf availability changes
a determinant is found to interact with another more strongly than modeled

nodes.definition: Establish pilling as the #1 post-purchase complaint and the main return driver, and the mechanism that lets four levers control it. Pilling is tangled balls of broken/loose surface fibres; it is worst with short, fine, low-twist, loosely-knit, hairy yarn (mnemonic: short-fine-low-twist-loose-hairy). Acrylic — the A2 value article and Ludhiana's base fibre — is the worst offender and is exactly where the spec must defend hardest; cashmere also pills more than wool. The four joint controls are fibre (staple, fineness, anti-pill grade), twist (higher binds surface fibres), gauge (tight knit + high stitch density resists pill formation), and anti-pill finish (cellulase bio-polish / singe / heat-set). The decisive honesty point: a low-pill yarn can be undone by a loose knit, so the control is joint across fibre+twist+gauge+finish, never any one alone.

included: pilling as the top return driver
the four joint controls and acrylic-as-worst-offender
excluded: the lever pull-order (its own node)
the contractual pilling gate (its own node)

pros.claim: Framing pilling as jointly controlled stops a single-lever fix that a loose knit then undoes
pros.example: a high-dpf anti-pill acrylic still pills if knit loose, so the gauge lever must be set with the fibre lever

cons.claim: Joint control means no single clause guarantees the outcome, so the gate must be empirical not predictive
cons.example: specifying all four levers still requires a post-wash swatch test to confirm the grade

nodes.definition: Order the pilling-defence levers most-controllable-first so the spec spends effort where it pays: longer staple -> higher twist -> ply (2-ply over singles) -> anti-pill / higher-dpf grade (the single biggest lever for acrylic) -> a few % nylon (for soft wool/cashmere blends, the cheapest pill+abrasion lever) -> lower hairiness (compact / air-jet spun) -> tight gauge + high stitch density (do not let a loose knit undo a low-pill yarn — carried to T3/T8) -> finishing (singe / cellulase bio-polish / heat-set — T6). Honesty discipline survives into the prose: vendor case studies claim anti-pill grades cut returns ~30-50% and compact spinning cuts shedding ~30%, so keep the DIRECTION (these levers materially help, HIGH confidence) but distrust the exact % (single-vendor, not independent trials) and never promise a customer a number. [ESTIMATE: industry-lore; direction HIGH, magnitude LOW-MED].

excluded: the per-article tier targets (its own node)
the recomputed risk score (its own node)

pros.claim: Ordering levers by control directs spec effort to the highest-leverage acrylic dial first
pros.example: switching to an anti-pill higher-dpf acrylic grade beats fiddling twist when A2 is the failure point

cons.claim: A fixed order can mislead when an article's binding lever is lower in the list (e.g. gauge on a loose style)
cons.example: for an intentionally loose A1 knit the gauge lever, not the fibre grade, may be the binding control

nodes.definition: Treat the blend ratio as the brand's #1 controllable lever and a duty-and-cheat risk surface. The ratio on the care label moves cost, hand, warmth, care, perceived value, and US import duty simultaneously (wool 6110.11 ~16% vs cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, with acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% the outlier the border penalizes [FACT - USITC duty lines]); even 5-10% cashmere lifts perceived value, and a few % nylon in a soft wool/cashmere blend is the cheapest pill+abrasion improvement. Because it is also a cheat-and-duty surface, it must be written into the PO with a tolerance — e.g. 70/30 +/- 3% by mass, verified by fibre-composition test. Blend drift (the supplier quietly shifting toward the cheaper fibre) is both a silent cost-down on us and, as importer of record, a duty-misdeclaration exposure; the +/- tolerance plus the composition-verify clause is the only enforcement. [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, HIGH on the lever; FACT on the duty lines].

excluded: which blend each article uses (fibre-line kb1)

pros.example: 70/30 +/- 3% verified by composition test lets a lab spot-check reject a drifted lot and protects the import declaration

cons.claim: A composition test per lot adds cost and lead time a micro-brand must budget
cons.example: third-party fibre-composition verification on every lot is a recurring QC line, not free

ignoring that drift toward wool/animal fibre also mis-declares duty as importer of record

nodes.definition: Define the evenness and point-defect metrics the PO grades against and why each predicts a knitting failure. CV% (CVm, coefficient of variation of mass) is the headline evenness number — lower = more even, cleaner knitting, fewer stops; legacy U% converts as CV% ~= 1.25 x U%. IPI (Imperfection Index) = thin (-50%) + thick (+50%) + neps (+200%) per 1000 m at standard sensitivities — the point-defect/cleanliness number, where a thin place breaks in knitting and shows as a light streak, a thick place shows as a heavy fault, and a nep is a visible speck worse with short/immature fibre. Hairiness (H / S3) — protruding fibre ends — drives pilling, hand and shed/lint, so spec a band (too high pills + dusts; too low looks flat/harsh). Count-CV — lot-to-lot and within-lot count drift — shifts GSM and shade between batches. Tenacity (cN/tex, ISO 2062) + elongation — low strength breaks in knitting (downtime) and weakens seams. Together these are the numbers a USTER report and a reject decision actually turn on.

included: CV%/CVm, IPI triplet at sensitivities, hairiness H/S3, count-CV, tenacity
excluded: the USTER percentile mapping (its own node)
the AQL sampling that draws the test lots (its own node)

pros.claim: Pinning each metric to a knitting failure makes the spec testable, not decorative
pros.example: a count-CV ceiling catches batch-to-batch GSM/shade drift before it shows in finished panels

cons.claim: A micro-brand cannot generate these numbers in-house, so they only bind if the spinner or a lab reports them
cons.example: an IPI ceiling is unenforceable against a micro-spinner that cannot produce a USTER report

ignoring count-CV so cross-run GSM/shade drift passes uncaught

nodes.definition: Set the USTER percentile language as the PO grading vocabulary and the achievable bar. A yarn is graded against USTER STATISTICS percentiles: 25% USTER = better than 75% of world production on a parameter, 5% USTER = top-5% world-class. The clause: demand <= 25% USTER on CVm% + IPI (with the thin/thick/nep sensitivities, a hairiness band, a minimum tenacity and a count-CV ceiling) on mainstream acrylic and cotton. The binding honesty: NEVER demand 5% USTER on a mass acrylic lot — 5% USTER on a mainstream lot is unquotable or luxury-priced, so a 5% clause either gets refused or silently re-priced as premium. 25% USTER is the mainstream bar; reserve any tighter percentile for a genuinely premium count where the spinner can quote it. [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, MED-HIGH that 25% is the right mainstream bar; FACT on the percentile definition].

included: the <=25% USTER on CVm%+IPI mainstream clause
excluded: the raw metric definitions (its own node)
the over-tighten guard across all dials (its own node)

pros.claim: Anchoring on 25% USTER gives an enforceable, quotable bar instead of an unattainable or vague one
pros.example: <=25% USTER on CVm% + IPI is a clause a Vardhman/Nahar-class spinner can actually certify

cons.claim: A percentile clause is only meaningful against the same USTER STATISTICS edition and parameter set both parties reference
cons.example: two parties citing different USTER editions can disagree on what 25% means for the same lot

acceptance_tests: the percentile method is stated, <=25% USTER on CVm% + IPI is set as the mainstream-acrylic/cotton bar, and 5% USTER on mass acrylic is explicitly ruled out as unquotable/luxury-priced

nodes.definition: Define the contractual pilling gate that makes an anti-pill claim real. Gate every anti-pill claim on the ICI Pilling Box test (ISO 12945-1) at grade >= 3-4 after >= 1 home-wash cycle. The post-wash condition is load-bearing: washing drops the pilling grade, and the post-wash grade — not the dry off-loom grade — is what predicts returns, so a dry-graded anti-pill claim is meaningless. The gate is run on a PPS swatch in the exact construction (fibre x twist x gauge), because pilling is jointly controlled and only the finished construction reveals the real grade. An adjective (anti-pill, low-pill) in a PO with no ICI post-wash number is unenforceable; the number is the contract. This is the gap the T5 thread-checker is meant to close cheaply by grading the pilling subset and sending a code back to the supplier.

included: the ICI Pilling Box ISO 12945-1 grade >= 3-4 gate
excluded: the lever order that produces the grade (its own node)
the AQL sample the swatch is drawn under (its own node)

pros.claim: A post-wash ICI number turns anti-pill from an adjective into a rejectable contract term
pros.example: a lot grading 2-3 after one wash fails the >= 3-4 gate and is rejected regardless of its dry grade

cons.claim: A post-wash swatch test adds sampling lead time and cost before bulk can be released
cons.example: waiting on a wash-and-grade cycle delays the PP approval a rushed drop calendar resents

failure_modes: accepting a dry off-loom pilling grade as the gate
writing anti-pill with no ICI number or no post-wash condition, leaving it unenforceable
acceptance_tests: the gate is ICI Pilling Box (ISO 12945-1) grade >= 3-4 after >= 1 home-wash cycle, the post-wash-predicts-returns rationale is stated, and the swatch-in-exact-construction requirement is named
revisit_triggers: a standard revision changes the ICI method or grade scale
return data shows the >= 3-4 bar is too lax or too strict for a tier
a new finish shifts the achievable post-wash grade

base.update_signal: a pilling standard, return signal, or finish shifts the gate

nodes.definition: Assemble the enforceable spec sheet attached to every yarn PO — the contract that replaces in-house metrology. The clause stack: fibre + blend (micron ceiling / anti-pill dpf, +/-% by mass, fibre-composition verified) - count (Ne/Nm folded + Tex in brackets; singles / ply / ends-fed) - twist (TPM + S/Z or K, balanced ply) - min staple - USTER clause (<= 25% USTER on CVm% + IPI + sensitivities; hairiness band; min tenacity; count-CV ceiling) - pilling acceptance (ICI >= 3-4 post-wash) - colour (shade std, lot-to-lot delta-E, fastness minima) - the GG + GSM / g-per-garment it must knit at - AQL sampling + reject rule - commercials (Incoterm, MOQ, lead time, price - to T9/kb2). The posture is contractual QC, not in-house metrology: a USTER-class tester is six-figure-USD class (exact list price [UNKNOWN]), so the brand enforces through the spinner's lab, third-party spot-checks and this PO, never owned equipment.

excluded: the commercials/landed-cost detail (T9/kb2)

nodes.definition: Define how AQL (Acceptable Quality Limit) sampling turns the spec into an accept/reject decision on a real lot. An AQL inspection plan sets a sample size drawn from the lot and an accept/reject number: the lot is accepted if defects in the sample stay at or below the accept number and rejected once they exceed it, at a chosen AQL level for major vs minor defects. For yarn, the sample feeds the USTER report, the composition test and the ICI post-wash pilling swatch; a breach of any hard gate (USTER percentile, ICI grade, composition tolerance) in the sample rejects the lot. The reject rule is the teeth of the spec: without a stated sample size and accept/reject number, the USTER and pilling clauses are advisory, not contractual. AQL is the standard buyer/third-party inspection gate on export orders and is detailed operationally in T5.

nodes.definition: Define the formula node that scores expected pilling/return risk against the spec dials and recomputes when any dial moves. The index combines the controllable dials into an expected post-wash pilling grade and a relative return-risk estimate: risk RISES with shorter staple, finer fibre/lower dpf, lower twist, singles over ply, looser gauge/lower stitch density, higher hairiness, and absence of anti-pill finish; risk FALLS as each dial is set toward its low-pill setting. Concretely, expected_pilling_grade is read up from the dial settings (longer staple + higher twist + 2-ply + anti-pill dpf + tight gauge + finish -> higher grade), and relative_return_risk is the inverse, normalized so the worst-case bare acrylic singles loose-knit sits high and a defended construction sits low. The score recomputes whenever a dial changes — improving the acrylic dpf or tightening the gauge lowers the predicted return risk and raises the predicted ICI grade. The magnitude is a labeled [ESTIMATE] (directionally HIGH-confidence from the lever mechanism, magnitude LOW-MED and unverified until a PPS swatch is ICI-tested); it is a planning dial, never a number promised to a customer, and the post-wash ICI swatch (PILLING_ACCEPTANCE_GATE) is the empirical check that confirms or corrects it.

nodes.definition: Guard against over-tightening the spec into an unquotable or counter-productive demand. Each dial has an optimum, not a maximum: demanding 5% USTER on mainstream acrylic is unquotable or luxury-priced (USTER_PERCENTILE_CLAUSE); demanding the finest possible micron makes the yarn softer but weaker and MORE pilling-prone (the counter-intuitive fineness dial); demanding maximum twist makes the yarn wiry and biases the fabric (spirality); a too-tight count-CV or hairiness band a mainstream spinner cannot certify just gets refused. Set each dial to its tier optimum — knitwear-soft twist ~ K3 with balanced ply, <= 25% USTER, a micron ceiling (not floor), an anti-pill dpf (not the finest dpf), a hairiness band (not minimum) — so the spec is both protective and quotable. The failure this prevents is a spec so tight it is either refused, silently re-priced as luxury, or actively worse for hand and durability.

included: dial-optimum-not-maximum across USTER, micron, twist, count-CV, hairiness
excluded: the per-article targets themselves (its own node)
the percentile clause definition (its own node)

pros.claim: Setting dials to optimum keeps the spec quotable and avoids actively harming hand/durability
pros.example: a micron ceiling protects softness without the over-fine, weaker, more-pilling yarn a micron floor would force

cons.claim: An optimum-not-maximum stance can read as accepting less than best and needs the rationale stated
cons.example: a buyer wanting the finest micron must be shown why that yarn pills more and is weaker

failure_modes: over-tightening to 5% USTER / finest micron / max twist and getting refused or a worse yarn

nodes.definition: Define the colour acceptance clauses that ride alongside the structural quality gates, because bought-dyed stock-shade buying carries lot-to-lot shade-match risk. Specify a shade standard (physical or instrumental), a lot-to-lot delta-E tolerance (the measured colour difference between dye lots a buyer will accept before rejecting), and fastness minima (wash, light, rub/crocking) so colour does not bleed, fade, or transfer in the finished sweater. These clauses are the structural-quality analogue on the colour axis: an even, low-pill yarn that shifts shade between lots still produces a returnable garment. Colour acceptance is lighter-weight than the USTER/ICI gates but belongs in the same PO, and it is the mitigation for the dyed-yarn lot-to-lot risk carried from the sourcing decision (kb2): launch on bought-dyed stock shades, and let the delta-E + fastness clauses, not trust, manage shade consistency.

included: shade standard, lot-to-lot delta-E, fastness minima (wash/light/rub)
excluded: the dyed-vs-greige sourcing decision (kb2)
the dyehouse regulatory risk (kb2/T1)

pros.claim: Delta-E and fastness clauses turn shade-match from trust into a rejectable term on stock-shade buys
pros.example: a second dye lot exceeding the delta-E tolerance is rejected rather than blended into stock and noticed by customers

cons.claim: Colour clauses add an instrumental shade-check step a micro-brand may not be equipped to run
cons.example: verifying delta-E lot-to-lot needs a spectrophotometer or a lab the brand does not own

failure_modes: omitting a lot-to-lot delta-E so stock-shade restocks drift in colour
specifying shade but not fastness, so colour bleeds or crocks in wear
acceptance_tests: a shade standard, a lot-to-lot delta-E tolerance, and wash/light/rub fastness minima are specified as PO clauses tied to the bought-dyed lot-to-lot risk
revisit_triggers: a restock lot drifts in shade
a fastness failure shows in wear or wash

base.update_signal: a shade drift, fastness failure, or dye-method change updates the clause

nodes.definition: Map each yarn-stage defect to the finished-garment defect and return it causes, closing the loop from spec to customer. Thin places -> light streaks + knitting breaks; thick places + neps -> visible heavy faults/specks; high CV% -> streaky, uneven fabric + knitting stops (scrap + downtime); unbalanced singles twist -> skew/torque -> spirality, the twisted-side-seam defect + a QC reject; low tenacity -> breaks in knitting + weak seams; high hairiness + short/fine/low-twist fibre -> pilling (the top return driver); count drift -> GSM + shade shift between batches; over-milling -> irreversible shrink/felt. This linkage is why the upstream metrics are worth speccing: every USTER number and the ICI gate trace to a specific garment defect and a specific return reason, so the spec is justified by the failure it prevents, not by metrology for its own sake.

excluded: the metric definitions (its own node)
the finishing treatments that fix some defects (T6)

pros.claim: Tracing each metric to a garment defect justifies the spec by the return it prevents
pros.example: speccing balanced ply is justified by preventing the spirality/twisted-side-seam return, not by abstract twist control

cons.claim: Some yarn-to-garment links are construction-dependent, so the map is directional not deterministic
cons.example: whether a given hairiness causes pilling depends on the gauge it is knit at

failure_modes: speccing a metric with no garment-defect rationale, so it gets value-engineered out
missing the unbalanced-twist -> spirality link and accepting a skewing yarn
acceptance_tests: each major yarn defect (thin/thick/nep, CV%, unbalanced twist, low tenacity, hairiness, count drift) is mapped to its finished-garment defect and return reason
revisit_triggers: a return reason traces to an unmapped yarn defect
a construction change alters a defect linkage
a finishing step removes a previously load-bearing defect

base.update_signal: a return reason or construction change updates a defect linkage

nodes.definition: Frame the cost-of-quality economics that justify the spec spend: the marginal cost of a tighter dial (anti-pill dpf premium, higher twist, 25% USTER certification, per-lot ICI swatch + AQL inspection, third-party test fallback) is traded against the cost of the failure it prevents (a return, a markdown, a damaged D2C reputation, a duty-misdeclaration penalty). Yarn fibre itself is small and well-anchored (~$1-2.50 of fibre per sweater [ESTIMATE, MED-HIGH]) so it is NOT the binding cost; the binding cost is the failure tail, where pilling drives the #1 return reason. The spec spend is justified where the prevented-return cost exceeds the dial-cost — heaviest on A2 acrylic (worst pilling) and on the blend-ratio composition test (duty exposure). The economics are an [ESTIMATE]: the dial premiums and the third-party test cost are bands with stated confidence, and the return-rate reduction direction is HIGH but the magnitude LOW-MED (vendor claims, not independent trials), so the trade-off is computed with labeled estimates and refused as fake-precise.

excluded: the full landed-cost / margin model (T9)
the recompute mechanics of the risk index (its own node)

pros.example: the anti-pill dpf premium on A2 is justified because the prevented pilling-return cost exceeds it

cons.claim: The return-rate reduction magnitude is vendor-sourced, so the trade-off is directional not precisely sized

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every money/capacity/performance/regulation claim in this spec: tag each [FACT] (cited public source or true-by-definition identity), [ESTIMATE] (method + basis + confidence, carrying the literal word estimate), or [UNKNOWN] (genuinely not known, a valid and frequent value). nodes.definition: Produce the lot accept/reject verdict that composes every gate into one decision. The merged rule: a received yarn lot is accepted only if it clears all hard gates in the AQL sample — <= 25% USTER on CVm% + IPI (with sensitivities, hairiness band, min tenacity, count-CV ceiling), ICI Pilling Box grade >= 3-4 after >= 1 home-wash on the construction swatch, fibre composition within the +/- tolerance, and colour delta-E + fastness within clause — and is rejected the moment it fails any one hard gate, regardless of the others. A demand-true commercial (good price, fast lead time, flexible MOQ) never overrides a failed quality gate; an untestable lot (micro-spinner with no report) is treated as a fail until a third-party test is run. This is the teeth that turn the spec sheet into an accept/reject machine, with the pilling and USTER gates as the load-bearing pair and the composition/colour gates as the duty and shade backstops.

edges.resolution_rule: set each dial to its tier optimum (<=25% USTER, micron ceiling, K3 twist, hairiness band); never tighten to a level a mainstream spinner cannot quote, and reserve 5% USTER for a genuinely premium count only

edges.why_related: the cost-of-quality trade-off weighs the dial spend against the return risk the index predicts
the labeled-estimate dial-premium and return-rate bands constrain the trade-off to direction, not fake-precise breakeven
the guardrail governs how the percentile bands and tester-price unknowns may be expressed
the verdict consumes the USTER clause as a hard gate
the verdict consumes the ICI post-wash pilling gate as a hard gate
the verdict applies the AQL sample and reject rule to draw and judge the lot
the verdict applies the composition +/- tolerance as a hard gate
the verdict applies the colour delta-E/fastness clause as a shade backstop gate
the verdict must express any commercial rationale as a labeled estimate under the guardrail
the predicted risk must not override an empirical gate result: a swatch that fails the ICI gate rejects regardless of a low predicted score
the review loop watches the gate inputs to the verdict and re-triggers it when they change
a divergent PPS swatch ICI result sends the analysis back to recalibrate the risk index
a swatch fail or dpf-availability change re-runs the affected article's dial targets
the verdict must reject defects that map to returns even when a commercial pressures acceptance

conflict_axes.name: quality_gate_vs_commercial_terms
conflict_axes.description: A lot can carry an attractive price, lead time or MOQ flexibility yet fail a hard quality gate (USTER, ICI post-wash, composition), so the commercial and quality views point opposite ways.
poles: reject on the failed quality gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: a failed hard gate rejects the lot regardless of price/lead-time/MOQ; commercials never override quality

conflict_axes.name: tighter_spec_vs_quotability
conflict_axes.description: A tighter dial (5% USTER, finest micron, max twist, very tight count-CV) protects quality but can be unquotable, luxury-priced, or actively worse for hand/durability.
poles: loosen to the quotable tier optimum
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set each dial to its tier optimum (<=25% USTER, micron ceiling, K3 twist); never tighten past what a mainstream spinner can quote

conflict_axes.name: finer_softer_vs_more_pilling
conflict_axes.description: Finer fibre (lower micron / lower dpf) is softer and more premium-feeling but is weaker and pills MORE, so the softness and durability goals pull against each other.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spec a micron ceiling (animal) or anti-pill dpf (synthetic) that balances softness against the pilling/strength penalty, confirmed by the post-wash ICI swatch

conflict_axes.name: higher_twist_vs_soft_hand
conflict_axes.description: Higher twist binds surface fibres and cuts pilling but makes the yarn wiry and harsh and can bias the fabric (spirality), trading pilling control against the hand the customer feels.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: target knitwear-soft twist ~ K3 with balanced ply — enough to bind fibres without a wiry hand or spirality

conflict_axes.name: predicted_risk_vs_empirical_gate
conflict_axes.description: The recomputed pilling-risk index can read low while the actual post-wash ICI swatch grades below the gate, so the model and the measurement can disagree.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the empirical post-wash ICI swatch always overrides the predicted score; the index is a planning dial, the swatch is the gate

conflict_axes.name: blend_value_vs_drift_and_duty
conflict_axes.description: A richer/cheaper blend ratio lifts value or margin but invites blend drift, a silent cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration exposure as importer of record.
poles: lock the ratio with tolerance + composition verify
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: write the ratio with a +/-% tolerance and a fibre-composition test so value optimization cannot become uncontrolled drift or duty exposure

conflict_axes.name: moq_flexibility_vs_testability
conflict_axes.description: Micro-spinners flex MOQ further but cannot self-test, so the lowest-MOQ vendor is often the one that cannot certify a quality-gated lot.
poles: route gated orders to testable capacity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: send any quality-gated article to a USTER-equipped spinner or budget a third-party spot-check; treat untestable capacity as a disqualifier for gated lots

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] labeling of dial premiums, return rates and tester prices protects honesty but can make the spec read as too hedged to act on.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure but pair it with a confidence and a confirmation path (live quote, PPS swatch) so the spec stays actionable without overclaiming

conflict_axes.name: fibre_cost_vs_failure_tail_cost
conflict_axes.description: Fibre per sweater is small and well-anchored, tempting a focus on shaving fibre cost, while the binding cost is the failure tail (pilling returns, markdowns) that the dial spend prevents.
poles: spend on the dials that cut the failure tail
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat fibre as small-not-binding and direct quality spend to the dials (anti-pill dpf, gauge, composition test) whose prevented-failure cost exceeds the dial cost

edge_cases.description: A lot is accepted on a dry off-loom pilling grade that passes, then pills below grade after one home wash
edge_cases.trigger: the pilling gate is read before any wash cycle
edge_cases.mitigation: gate only on the ICI Pilling Box grade >= 3-4 after >= 1 home-wash on the construction swatch, never on the dry grade

edge_cases.description: 5% USTER is demanded on a mainstream acrylic lot and the spinner refuses or re-prices it as luxury
edge_cases.trigger: an over-tight USTER percentile is written for a mass acrylic article
edge_cases.mitigation: hold <= 25% USTER on CVm% + IPI for mainstream acrylic/cotton; reserve any tighter percentile for a genuinely premium count

edge_cases.description: A quality-gated USTER/ICI clause is enforced against a micro-spinner that cannot self-test
edge_cases.trigger: a gated order is placed with untestable capacity on verbal assurance
edge_cases.mitigation: route the gated order to a USTER-equipped spinner or budget a third-party per-lot spot-check; treat the untestable lot as a fail until tested

edge_cases.description: Blend drift toward the cheaper fibre passes uncaught and mis-declares import duty
edge_cases.trigger: the ratio is specced with no tolerance or composition test
edge_cases.mitigation: write the ratio with a +/-% by-mass tolerance and a fibre-composition test, and reject a lot outside tolerance

edge_cases.description: An anti-pill claim in the PO is an adjective with no ICI number, so it is unenforceable
edge_cases.trigger: anti-pill or low-pill is written without an ICI post-wash grade
edge_cases.mitigation: replace every anti-pill adjective with an ICI Pilling Box grade >= 3-4 post-wash number

edge_cases.description: The predicted pilling-risk score reads low but the post-wash ICI swatch grades below the gate
edge_cases.trigger: the risk index is trusted in place of the empirical swatch
edge_cases.mitigation: let the post-wash ICI swatch override the predicted score; reject the lot and recalibrate the index

edge_cases.description: A 2/30 folded count is read as 1/30 (or vice versa), doubling the assumed fabric weight
edge_cases.trigger: folded-count notation is judged without confirming singles + ply + ends-fed
edge_cases.mitigation: always confirm singles count + ply + ends-fed (Ne/Nm folded + Tex) before judging weight or gauge

edge_cases.description: An unbalanced singles twist produces spirality / a twisted side seam in the finished panel
edge_cases.trigger: balanced ply is not required in the PO
edge_cases.mitigation: require balanced ply (opposing S/Z twists) and reject a skewing/torquing yarn at sampling

edge_cases.description: A finer micron is specced to maximize softness and the yarn comes back weaker and more pilling-prone
edge_cases.trigger: a micron floor (finest) rather than a ceiling is written
edge_cases.mitigation: spec a micron ceiling that balances softness against the strength/pilling penalty, confirmed by the ICI swatch

edge_cases.description: A bought-dyed restock lot drifts in shade and is blended into stock, surfacing as a customer-visible mismatch
edge_cases.trigger: no lot-to-lot delta-E tolerance is specified for stock-shade buys
edge_cases.mitigation: specify a lot-to-lot delta-E tolerance + fastness minima and reject a restock lot outside tolerance

edge_cases.description: A vendor's ~30-50% anti-pill return-reduction claim is promised to a customer as a guaranteed number
edge_cases.trigger: a single-vendor magnitude claim is treated as an independent fact
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the direction (levers help, HIGH) but hold the magnitude LOW-MED and never promise a customer a return-reduction number

edge_cases.description: A third-party lab or USTER-tester cost is fabricated as a precise figure to complete a cost model
edge_cases.trigger: the UNKNOWN lab/tester price is filled with an invented point
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the lab/tester cost as [UNKNOWN] / labeled estimate band and refuse a point until a live quote lands

workflow.description: Record staple, twist, ply, micron/dpf, blend ratio and each dial's customer-felt outcome with its direction
workflow.gate: all five dials are named with direction and the finer=softer-but-pills-more caveat stated

workflow.action: Establish the pilling mechanism and joint controls
workflow.description: State pilling as the top return driver and the four joint controls, flagging acrylic as worst
workflow.gate: pilling is the top return driver, the five causes and four controls are named, acrylic flagged worst

workflow.description: List levers most-controllable-first with the anti-pill dpf as the biggest acrylic lever
workflow.gate: levers ordered most-controllable-first with vendor-claim direction-vs-magnitude discipline stated

workflow.description: Define CV%, the IPI triplet at sensitivities, hairiness, count-CV, tenacity with their knitting failures
workflow.gate: each metric is defined with the thin/thick/nep sensitivities and the failure it predicts

workflow.description: Set <= 25% USTER on CVm% + IPI as the mainstream bar and rule out 5% USTER on mass acrylic
workflow.gate: the percentile method is stated, 25% is the bar, and 5% on mass acrylic is ruled out as unquotable

workflow.description: Gate on ICI Pilling Box grade >= 3-4 after >= 1 home-wash on the construction swatch
workflow.gate: the ICI >= 3-4 post-wash gate and the post-wash-predicts-returns rationale are stated

workflow.action: Lock the blend ratio with tolerance and verify
workflow.description: Write the ratio with a +/-% by-mass tolerance and a fibre-composition test against drift and duty exposure
workflow.gate: the ratio is tied to cost/duty, drift is flagged, and the +/-% + composition-verify clause is specified

workflow.action: Assemble the enforceable PO spec sheet
workflow.description: Compose the full clause stack and state the contractual-QC-not-metrology posture
workflow.gate: the clause stack enumerates fibre/count/twist/staple/USTER/pilling/colour/GG-GSM/AQL/commercials with the posture stated

workflow.action: Set AQL sampling and the reject rule
workflow.description: Define the sample size, accept/reject number, and the any-hard-gate-breach-rejects rule
workflow.gate: a sample size and accept/reject number exist and a hard-gate breach in the sample rejects the lot

workflow.description: Map A1/A2/A3 to their own staple/twist/dpf-or-micron/USTER/pilling targets
workflow.gate: each article has its own dial targets with A2 hardest on anti-pill and A3 on the micron ceiling

workflow.description: Combine USTER, ICI post-wash, composition, colour and AQL into one accept/reject call
workflow.gate: the verdict rejects on any hard-gate fail and refuses commercial override and untestable lots

workflow.action: Set the quality review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the refresh cadence and material-change triggers routing back to the risk score and spec
workflow.gate: a cadence and trigger list (PPS-swatch ICI highest-leverage) routing to PILLING_RISK_SCORE and the spec exist

dominance_rules.rule: A failed hard quality gate dominates any attractive commercial term
dominance_rules.rationale: a cheap, fast, or low-MOQ lot that pills or fails USTER still produces returns
dominance_rules.trigger: a lot fails a hard gate but carries a good price/lead-time/MOQ
dominance_rules.action: reject the lot on the failed gate regardless of the commercial terms

dominance_rules.rule: The post-wash ICI swatch dominates the predicted pilling-risk score
dominance_rules.rationale: the index is a planning estimate while the swatch is the empirical gate
dominance_rules.trigger: the predicted risk reads low but the post-wash swatch grades below the gate
dominance_rules.action: reject on the swatch and recalibrate the risk index

dominance_rules.rule: The dial optimum dominates a tighter maximum
dominance_rules.rationale: 5% USTER, finest micron, or max twist is unquotable or actively worse for hand/durability
dominance_rules.trigger: a dial is tightened past the tier optimum
dominance_rules.action: set the dial to its tier optimum (<=25% USTER, micron ceiling, K3 twist) and refuse the over-tight maximum

dominance_rules.rule: Testable capacity dominates micro-spinner MOQ flexibility for gated articles
dominance_rules.rationale: an untestable lot cannot certify a quality gate
dominance_rules.trigger: a quality-gated order is offered to a micro-spinner that cannot self-test
dominance_rules.action: route to a USTER-equipped spinner or budget a third-party test; treat untestable as a fail

dominance_rules.rule: The composition test dominates a verbal blend assurance
dominance_rules.rationale: blend drift is a silent cost-down and a duty exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: a blend ratio is accepted on supplier assurance without a tolerance or test
dominance_rules.action: require the +/-% tolerance + fibre-composition test and reject a lot outside tolerance

dominance_rules.rule: The failure-tail cost dominates the small fibre cost in quality spend
dominance_rules.rationale: fibre is ~$1-2.50/garment while the binding cost is the pilling-return tail
dominance_rules.trigger: quality spend is directed at shaving fibre cost instead of the anti-pill dial
dominance_rules.action: direct spend to the dials whose prevented-failure cost exceeds the dial cost

dominance_rules.rule: A labeled estimate dominates a fake-precise figure for any price/MOQ/throughput/lab claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no live quote exists, so a precise point would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a dial premium, MOQ, throughput, lead time, or lab/tester price is stated as a precise fact
dominance_rules.action: express it as an [ESTIMATE] band with confidence + confirmation path, or [UNKNOWN] until quoted

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the risk score or a cost-of-quality estimate carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the confirmation source (PPS swatch / live quote)

anti_rework_rules.rule: Catalog the five spinning dials before writing any clause or tier target
anti_rework_rules.prevents: writing clauses against an incomplete dial set that must be re-specced when a dial is added

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate pilling on the post-home-wash ICI grade from the first draft, never the dry grade
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a spec that passes on dry grade then fails in the field, forcing a full anti-pill re-spec

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write every price/MOQ/throughput/lab figure as a labeled estimate or UNKNOWN at the moment it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already written as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the USTER percentile to the achievable mainstream bar (<=25%) before pricing the lot
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a 5%-USTER clause that gets refused or luxury-re-priced and forces re-quoting

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm singles count + ply + ends-fed before judging weight or gauge
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a 2/30-vs-1/30 doubling error that mis-sizes the whole article and forces a re-spec

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route a quality-gated order to testable capacity while selecting the vendor, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: placing a gated order with a micro-spinner that then cannot certify it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock the blend ratio with a tolerance and a composition test the first time the blend is specced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: blend drift passing uncaught into a duty-misdeclaration or silent cost-down that must be remediated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate the predicted pilling-risk score against a PPS swatch ICI test before relying on it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a spec built on an unvalidated risk estimate that the field then contradicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a PPS swatch ICI result diverges from the predicted pilling grade
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the risk index and re-tune the affected article's dial targets

iteration_protocol.trigger: a return-rate signal from live sell-through lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the pilling gate and the cost-of-quality breakeven against the observed return rate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new USTER STATISTICS edition is released
iteration_protocol.action: re-baseline the percentile clause and re-grade the affected USTER thresholds

iteration_protocol.trigger: a pilling/tenacity/AQL standard is revised (ISO 12945 / ISO 2062 / AQL plan)
iteration_protocol.action: update the affected gate and reject rule to the revised standard

iteration_protocol.trigger: an anti-pill acrylic dpf grade becomes available or unavailable in-cluster
iteration_protocol.action: re-set the A2 acrylic dial targets and re-run its risk score

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live third-party lab or USTER-tester quote becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: harden the testability routing cost and the cost-of-quality bands from the quote

iteration_protocol.trigger: a duty line or surcharge change alters the blend's import exposure
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the blend-ratio duty exposure and re-check the composition tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a bought-dyed restock lot drifts in shade or fails fastness
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the colour delta-E/fastness clause and re-judge the affected lots

priority_rationale: The five spinning dials and the pilling mechanism are foundational because every clause, metric, tier target and the risk score read from them; the evenness/defect metrics and the USTER percentile clause precede the acceptance gates they feed; the pilling acceptance gate, blend-ratio clause and enforceable PO spec assemble the contract, with AQL sampling giving it teeth; the per-article tier spec and the pilling-risk score apply the dials per article and recompute over them; the cost-of-quality economics and the two placeholder/UNKNOWN nodes keep the money claims honest; the honesty guardrail governs every figure's expression; and the lot accept/reject verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all gates into a decision and a self-correcting refresh against the PPS-swatch ICI result.
